methodParagraphs: Providers are matched by `providerKey` and aggregated across the runs they appear in; sums and means cover present values only.

Quality ranks the unweighted mean `metrics.score` descending. Speed ranks aggregate pages per minute (`sum(pageCount) / sum(processingTimeMs / 60000)`) descending. Cost ranks USD per 100 pages (`sum(costCents) / sum(pageCount)`) ascending with local providers at zero. Weighted WER/CER are evidence: summed breakdown errors over summed reference counts. Missing values sort last; ties break deterministically.

Per-run WER uses ASCII [a-z0-9] tokens after normalization and excludes non-ASCII glyphs, including Japanese. Headline quality is WER-derived; assess Japanese and other non-Latin extraction with supporting Unicode CER and source-image review.

5 runs use partial annotated-word references with text-only OCR. They contribute cost and speed, but no primary quality score or weighted error counts. Annotated-target token coverage and derived-order WER/CER are separate diagnostics; they do not establish region localization or exhaustive full-page accuracy.
notes: Each provider is aggregated by providerKey across the runs it appears in; sums and means cover present values only.
Groups follow the single-run OCR contract: local, thirdPartyService; local and service providers are never ranked against each other.
Weighted WER and weighted CER are evidence columns: summed breakdown errors divided by summed reference counts, so longer runs count proportionally more.

Per-run WER tokenizes normalized text as ASCII [a-z0-9] runs and excludes non-ASCII glyphs, including Japanese. The WER-derived headline quality score does not measure complete Japanese or other non-Latin OCR accuracy.
CER retains normalized Unicode letters and numbers as supporting evidence. Review CER and the source images when assessing non-Latin extraction quality.
Each group ranks price, speed, and quality score independently. No weighted composite or model-tier ranking is emitted.
Supersedes the hand-authored 2026-06-14 combined report, which is preserved as a historical record.

notes: October 26 storage update: the user approved the MP3 playback copies and deletion of the final WAVs. The October 15 ASR and signal measurements describe the original WAVs; the current MP3s have not been reassessed.

October 15 assessment: all eight original WAV recordings received local ASR screening and signal analysis. Separate turn windows support descriptive measurements in six cases. Subjective voice-quality and audible-control ratings are excluded and unscored at the user's instruction; signal gaps and reference-word throughput do not establish semantic pause accuracy or calibrated numeric-speed effects.

The existing ElevenLabs pacing case was skipped because its exact tags were unverified for eleven_v3. OpenAI has no case in the existing controls plans. Both providers were included in all four narration inputs.

methodParagraphs: Narration rankings use the common direct-child TTS benchmark corpus. Controls are shown separately because providers expose different native mechanisms. Emotion and delivery, and speed and pauses, each select their newest dated standalone benchmark directory independently; earlier revisions are excluded.

User-approved MP3 playback copies are bound to original WAV hashes in tts/audio-delivery.json. Original synthesis manifests, render identities and generation costs remain unchanged. Assessment rows retain the exact audio hashes they measured; original-WAV rows are historical and never relabeled as MP3 assessments. Decoded sample counts, sample rates and channels were verified during conversion. Missing local MP3s retain their catalogued metadata and restore links; locally present copies must match their recorded hash.

Selected manifest audio references and SHA-256 hashes are authoritative. Original audio duration and format are read locally with ffprobe; approved MP3 copies use verified decoded sample counts and catalogued format, with local ffprobe verification when present. Current provider usage is preferred for cost, then recorded usage estimates, then the selected render estimate. Costs describe the selected synthesis, not all historical spending or confirmed invoices. Soniox costs remain estimates based on measured provider audio before local silence insertion.

Generation throughput is total final audio duration divided by total recorded generation time, including local assembly. Local recovery timings are labeled and excluded. Speed and cost rankings require complete narration coverage; timings reflect their original concurrency and machine conditions.

Automated accuracy is installed Whisper small.en roundtrip ASR screening: 100 × max(0, 1 − total word edits / total reference words), requiring every narration input. One recognizer can mishear speech, and literal number spellings remain differences. This is not acoustic adjudication. Controls remain separate unranked cases. Subjective pronunciation, speaker identity, emotion, seams/prosody, audible-control and perceptual ratings are excluded and unscored at the user’s instruction; see tts/assessment.md and its checksummed evidence archive.

Historical OpenAI benchmark costs retain their original character-based estimate and have not been retrospectively corrected to native text/audio-token billing. Recorded costs are not observed native billing receipts.
notes: Audio and evidence links are relative. Audio playback requires the retained local recordings. Refreshing this page makes no provider calls and does not alter benchmark artifacts.

model.title: Write benchmark results
methodParagraphs: Each model/provider route receives the same fixed input and preset within a prompt case. Comparisons select the latest completed attempt for each prompt/model pair, including a latest failure; earlier attempts remain in request evidence. The all-five table gives each prompt equal weight, averaging seconds/request and dollars/request only for routes with five valid outputs. A passing request requires explicitly recorded schema validation, a nonempty structured object without a failure envelope, and the saved output hash when a slot receipt exists. Missing, failed, corrupt, or schema-failed outputs remain visible without passing ranks.

Speed is metadata.step3.processingTime in wall-clock seconds/request, with lower values better. It includes generation and provider latency; it is not time to first token or a normalized token throughput score.

Usage-based cost is recorded token usage multiplied by uncached catalog tariffs, in USD/request (metadata.cost.actual.steps cents divided by 100). Cache discounts and Argon introductory pricing are excluded. Provider-usage and heuristic cost sources remain visible in the request evidence. Summary cost and unknown-billing counts are cumulative across all attempts, including superseded failed and invalid requests; ranking costs use only selected requests. Attempted slots with unknown cost are counted separately from unattempted missing routes. These calculations do not establish provider invoices or charged spend.

At the user's request, higher listed output-token price is a temporary quality proxy. The Price proxy ($ / 1M output tokens) column uses benchmark-plan.json's fixed rate snapshot, falling back to the run's estimated-cost rate snapshot when no plan rate exists. It is not measured text quality, an automated judge score, or a human assessment. Schema validity only determines whether a request is eligible for comparison.
notes: One selected request per model per prompt. These are single-run measurements; targeted failure reruns do not establish latency variability or medians.
The earlier September Write benchmark is preserved in its original directory and excluded from the five-prompt aggregate.
Request cost and output-token list price answer different questions: the price proxy is a model rate; dollars/request also depends on input length, generated output, reasoning usage, and caching.
